message.content:
Here’s a quick Python snippet that does exactly that:

```python
temp = "hello=good="
parts = temp.split('=', 1)   # split only on the first '='
print(parts)                # → ['hello', 'good=']
```

Using `split('=', 1)` tells Python to split at most once, so the remainder of the string (including any additional `=` characters) stays together in the second element.
